 Hon'Ble Praveen Kumar Giri, J.

1 .  Heard Mr. Akhileshwar Pratap Singh, learned counsel for the applicants and Mrs. Pushpa Joshi,
Advocate holding brief of Mr. Saurabh Yadav, learned counsel for opposite party No.2, wife of applicant No.1.
2. Learned counsel for the applicants submits that he has filed the instant application under Section 482 Cr.P.C. with the relief which has been mentioned in the prayer clause of the application.

3. The relief which has been mentioned in the application is delineated below:-
"It is, therefore, most respectfully prayed

that this Hon'ble Court may graciously be pleased to allow this application and quash the entire proceeding and quash the Charge sheet dated 05.09.2020 in Case No. 16269 of 2020 (State Vs. Ajay Chauhan and others) arising out case crime no.6 of 2020 under section 498A, 323, 506 I.P.C.
and section 3/4 Dowry Prohibition Act, Police Station Mahila Thana, District Budaun.

"
4. Learned counsel for opposite party No. 2 submits that during the divorce proceedings, both the parties entered into a compromise whereby it was agreed that all cases pending in any court of law,
either criminal or civil, shall be withdrawn and no further proceedings shall be initiated in future in this regard.

5. Learned counsel for the applicants submits that in paragraph No.5 of the supplementary affidavit,
it has been mentioned that some of the cases have already been dismissed on the basis of compromise.

Paragraph No. 5 of the supplementary affidavit is delineated below:
"That it is also submitted that except the present case opposite party No.2 filed some other cases against the applicants and other family members out of which one case being Complaint Case No.6727/22, under Section 420, 423, 323, 504, 506 IPC, P.S.
Civil Lines. District- Budaun, which was dismissed by the ACJ (Junior Division)
Court No.7/Judicial Magistrate Budaun, under Section 203 Cr.P.C. vide order dated 29.03.2022, the second case is under Section 125 Cr.P.C. P.S. Civil Lines, District- Budaun was also dismissed on default by the Principal Judge/Family Court Budaun vide order dated 18.04.2023, the third case is complaint case which was filed by the father of the opposite party No.2 against the applicants under Section 394, 397 IPC,
P.S. Civil Lines, District- Budaun, which is also dismissed under Section 203 IPC vide order dated 11.11.2021."
6.

Learned counsel for the applicant further submits that in paragraph No. 6 of the divorce order dated 07.02.2023, it has been categorically mentioned that both the parties shall withdraw all the pending cases in any court of law.
Paragraph No. 6 of the divorce order dated 07.02.2023 is being quoted below:

In view of the above facts and circumstances and in the interest of justice, this Court, invoking inherent jurisdiction as provided under Section 482 Cr.P.C. and considering the dictum of the Apex Court in re: B.S. Joshi and others Vs. State of Haryana and Another; 2003 (4) SCC 675, Gian Singh vs. State of Punjab (2012) 10 SCC 303; State of Rajasthan vs. Shambhu Kewat, (2014) 4 SCC 149;
State of Madhya Pradesh vs. Deepak (2014) 10 SCC 285; State of Madhya Pradesh vs. Manish (2015)
8 SCC 307; J.Ramesh Kamath vs. Mohana Kurup (2016) 12 SCC 179; State of Madhya Pradesh vs.
Rajveer Singh (2016) 12 SCC 471 and Parbatbhai Ahir vs. State of Gujarat (2017) 9 SCC 641, deems it appropriate to allow the prayer of the applicants.
